title: SILENCER: From Discovery to Mitigation of Self-Bias in LLM-as-Benchmark-Generator

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating the difference in the relative performance of a Large Language Model (LLM) when evaluated on benchmarks it generated itself versus its performance on human-annotated reference benchmarks.
Measuring the performance overestimation of a model on a human-constructed benchmark whose questions have been paraphrased by the model itself, isolating the effect of familiar linguistic patterns.

Measuring the performance overestimation on a benchmark built from the model's self-generated questions (paraphrased by a proxy to remove language style bias) with labels annotated by a proxy, isolating the model's preference for topics it excels in.

Measuring the performance overestimation on a benchmark constructed from human-written questions but using labels generated by the model itself, capturing the inflation caused by the model's tendency to repeat its own classification or reasoning mistakes.
